svg.title: reliable-push at a glance
svg.desc: Your backend sends pushes through FCM and APNs to an iPhone and an Android phone, as today. For each tracked push it generates a tracking id with the payload jar, registers the push with the reliable-push backend with a 1 s timeout, and always sends the push with that id. On the iPhone the Notification Service Extension saves DELIVERED, sends it once and hands the notification back within 2 s; on Android the SDK turns a data message into a local notification after saving DELIVERED. The tracking module in each app reports DELIVERED when the push arrives and READ when it is tapped. If the policy is not met before the timeout, the reliable-push worker calls your signed fallback webhook, and your fallback service sends an SMS or an email. A per-app circuit breaker stops the fallbacks of an app whose delivery tracking is missing, so an outage does not turn into a storm of needless SMS. The ops dashboard shows each app's circuit. The numbered steps light up one after the other.
svg.text: A sidecar: your backend keeps sending pushes (plus a payload jar and one register call). reliable-push only tracks them and triggers a fallback.
example: timeout 10 min, trigger window 20 min (the default)

text.tspan: event in time: done, no fallback
policy not met: webhook ⑤, retried after 1, 2, 4, 8 min
circuit open (tracking missing): expired, no call

svg.text: Policy NOT_DELIVERED is met by DELIVERED or READ · NOT_READ only by READ · policy and timeout never reach the device
